head.title: Iftar at Home Dubai: Menu, Timing & Cost Guide | myCHEF
head.meta_description: How to host iftar at home in Dubai: the menu order, exact timing to Maghrib, halal and food-safety rules, and what a private chef or caterer costs.
head.h1: Iftar at Home in Dubai: A Host's Menu, Timing & Cost Guide

opening_paragraph: Here is the short version. Hosting iftar at home in Dubai is a shared, unhurried meal timed to Maghrib, with myCHEF private-chef service from around AED 1,200 so you break your fast at the table. A caterer plans the courses, keeps the food halal and hot, and clears up afterwards. That leaves you free to sit with family and guests instead of watching the oven.

replace_in_block.block_on_your_page: What a Dubai iftar at home looks like
replace_in_block.new_heading: What a Dubai iftar at home looks like
new_paragraphs: A home iftar follows a familiar rhythm, not a rigid set menu. You break the fast the moment Maghrib is called, traditionally with dates and a glass of laban or water. Then you pause for the prayer before the meal proper begins. Soup, usually a lentil shorba or harira, eases people back into eating. After that comes the part guests remember. A generous shared spread lands: hot and cold mezze, grilled meats, saffron rice and warm bread, with Arabic sweets and coffee to close. Portions run big, because iftar is about abundance and hospitality. MyCHEF's Arabic specialist, Layla Hassan, builds a family iftar around that arc, so nothing reaches the table too early or too late.

replace_in_block.block_on_your_page: When should you serve iftar at home in Dubai?
replace_in_block.new_heading: When should you serve iftar at home in Dubai?
new_paragraphs: Serve the opening bite the instant Maghrib is called, not a minute before. Iftar timing shifts daily through Ramadan as sunset moves later. Gulf News puts Maghrib in Dubai at roughly 6:18pm in the first days of Ramadan 2026, drifting toward 6:32pm by the third week, and notes fasting runs 12 to 14 hours a day. That daily drift matters when you cook for a crowd. Dishes that need to land hot have to be timed to the call to prayer, not a fixed clock. A good caterer works backwards from Maghrib, sending the dates and soup out first while the mains rest and hold. Hosting iftar at home in Dubai is far calmer when someone else owns that countdown.

replace_in_block.block_on_your_page: Is home iftar catering in Dubai halal and safe?
replace_in_block.new_heading: Is home iftar catering in Dubai halal and safe?
new_paragraphs: Yes. Reputable home iftar catering in Dubai is fully halal, and licensed caterers work to the emirate's food-safety code. During Ramadan, Dubai Municipality runs dedicated inspection campaigns covering how food is transported, stored, prepared and displayed, and it requires hot food held above 65°C and cold below 5°C, per Gulf News . Food handlers wear gloves and head covers and carry health cards. At federal level, food safety sits under Federal Law No. 10 of 2015, as the UAE Government notes, and licensed businesses register on Dubai Municipality 's FoodWatch platform. MyCHEF is implementing a structured 12-stage partner verification and quality-assurance framework across its culinary partner network, covering trade licence and permitted activities, food-safety permits, Person-in-Charge and food-handler training documentation, allergen controls, and a chef and service-team assessment.

replace_in_block.block_on_your_page: What goes on an iftar menu at home?
replace_in_block.new_heading: What goes on an iftar menu at home?
new_paragraphs: Build the iftar menu in three acts: openers, a warm main spread, and dessert. For the openers, think dates, laban, soup and a cold mezze table of hummus, moutabel, fattoush and vine leaves. The centre of an Arabic iftar menu in Dubai usually leans on mixed grills, ouzi or machboos, grilled fish and saffron rice, rounded out with warm breads. Close with kunafa, umm ali, katayef and Arabic coffee. Not every host wants a fixed plated meal. An iftar buffet at home lets guests serve themselves at their own pace once the fast is broken. Plenty of hosts also want a lighter, modern angle, so a good chef will fold in salads, grilled vegetables and a few non-Arabic dishes. For more iftar ideas, our Iftar Catering page sets out sample menus.

replace_in_block.block_on_your_page: How much does iftar at home in Dubai cost?
replace_in_block.new_heading: How much does iftar at home in Dubai cost?
new_paragraphs: Costs scale with guest count, menu and whether a chef cooks on site. As a rough guide, a private-chef iftar for a small family starts from around AED 1,200, a mid-sized family iftar of a dozen or so guests sits nearer AED 2,400, and a larger catered spread with staffed service runs from about AED 4,500 upward. A more elaborate, multi-station luxury iftar at home can reach AED 5,500 and beyond once you add live grills, extended dessert tables and full serving staff. Drop-off is the other half of the market and it is priced per head, not per event: a delivered iftar spread starts at AED 90 per person and a staffed buffet at AED 120, with a minimum of 10 guests, 20 for a buffet, and a minimum order of AED 900. You handle the plating and the timing yourself, which is the trade. For an exact figure, iftar catering prices in Dubai are quoted per event. Share your date, headcount and venue, and myCHEF returns an itemised proposal, usually within one business day.

replace_in_block.block_on_your_page: Iftar meal boxes, platters and drop-off
replace_in_block.new_heading: Iftar meal boxes, platters and drop-off
new_paragraphs: A large share of Ramadan searching is for an iftar box rather than a chef, and it is worth separating two things that share the word. An individual iftar meal box is one person's meal packed and labelled to be handed out or eaten at a desk: dates, a soup, a main with rice, bread, a sweet and water. A drop-off platter feeds a table from shared trays. MyCHEF arranges both as delivered catering from AED 90 per person, with a minimum of 10 people and a minimum order of AED 900, and boxes are the easier format when guests arrive at different times or eat in different rooms. Ordering an iftar box near me on a Ramadan evening is mostly a question of lead time, so send the date early: a standard drop-off wants about 72 hours, and Ramadan weekends go first.

Iftar meal distribution is a different job again, and we would rather say so than take the enquiry. Distributing hundreds or thousands of meals to workers or through a charity is a volume operation that transacts near the cost of the ingredients, far below the AED 90 per person our smallest format starts at, and myCHEF has no product at that price. If that is your project, a high-volume production kitchen or a Ramadan charity programme will serve it properly and we will point you at that instead of quoting you something that does not fit. What we do handle well is the fifty-box office iftar and the family drop-off.

On iftar at home offers: what myCHEF publishes is a price list, not a seasonal discount. The same per-head tiers apply through Ramadan as through the rest of the year, which is deliberate — a Ramadan promotion usually means a headline figure with the service, equipment and delivery added back afterwards. The honest lever on cost is the format, so moving from a chef-attended dinner to a staffed buffet or a drop-off changes the number far more than any offer would.

replace_in_block.block_on_your_page: What makes a good iftar at home, and how to judge one
replace_in_block.new_heading: What makes a good iftar at home, and how to judge one
new_paragraphs: The best iftar at home in Dubai is not the most elaborate one; it is the one that lands on time. Judge a caterer or chef on four things. Do they plan backwards from Maghrib rather than from a fixed arrival time, so the dates and water are on the table before anyone sits? Will they tell you the dish count in writing, so you can compare two quotes instead of two adjectives? Is the price per head published with its minimum guest count attached, or does it appear only after you enquire? And who holds the food-safety responsibility for the kitchen the food comes from — a question that matters more in Ramadan, when food sits waiting for a sunset that moves a minute each evening. Ask those four and the choice usually makes itself.

replace_in_block.block_on_your_page: Private chef or caterer for your iftar?
replace_in_block.new_heading: Private chef or caterer for your iftar?
new_paragraphs: Choose a private chef when you want the food cooked fresh in your kitchen and served in courses. Choose a caterer when volume and self-service matter more. A private iftar in Dubai with a dedicated iftar chef suits intimate family nights, and anyone who wants each dish served at its freshest. Larger gatherings often work well as a buffet a caterer sets up, replenishes and clears. MyCHEF matches you to the right chef for the brief: Layla Hassan for a traditional Arabic family iftar, or another specialist if you want a fusion or lighter menu. Either way, you are not the one plating at sunset. Start from our private chef or catering in Dubai pages to compare the two formats.

replace_in_block.block_on_your_page: Planning an iftar party, or suhoor too
replace_in_block.new_heading: Planning an iftar party, or suhoor too
new_paragraphs: For a bigger iftar party at home, plan the space as carefully as the food. Majlis-style low seating, shared platters and a clear flow from the dates-and-soup opening to the main spread work better than a formal sit-down when numbers climb. Book early, because chefs fill up fast across Ramadan. Many hosts who cater iftar also add suhoor, the pre-dawn meal before the fast resumes. Suhoor at home in Dubai tends to be lighter and slower, built around foul, eggs, cheeses, fruit and plenty of water and laban to carry you through the fasting hours. MyCHEF can cover both ends of the day. See our Ramadan and Suhoor pages to plan the full month.

What time is iftar in Dubai during Ramadan 2026?

Iftar is served at Maghrib, sunset. In Dubai that falls at roughly 6:15 to 6:20pm in the first days of Ramadan 2026 and drifts a little later each evening, per Gulf News. Ramadan is expected to begin on 19 February 2026, subject to the moon sighting.
What should an iftar menu at home include?

Open with dates, laban and soup, then a shared spread of mezze, grilled meats and saffron rice, and finish with Arabic sweets and coffee. Keep portions generous, since iftar is a meal built around sharing.
How much does iftar at home in Dubai cost?

A delivered iftar spread or boxed meals start at AED 90 per person and a staffed buffet at AED 120, with a minimum of 10 guests, 20 for a buffet, and a minimum order of AED 900. A private-chef iftar for a small family starts from around AED 1,200, and larger staffed spreads run from about AED 4,500. The final figure depends on guest count, menu and service style, so myCHEF quotes each event individually.
Do you do iftar meal boxes?

Yes, as delivered catering from AED 90 per person with a 10-person minimum. Each box holds one person's meal, labelled: dates, soup, a main with rice, bread, a sweet and water. It is the easier format when guests arrive at different times or eat in different rooms. Large-scale iftar meal distribution to workers or through a charity transacts far below that tier, and myCHEF has no product at that price.
Is home iftar catering in Dubai halal?

Yes. Home iftar catering in Dubai is fully halal, and licensed caterers follow Dubai Municipality food-safety rules, including holding hot food above 65°C and cold below 5°C. MyCHEF is implementing a 12-stage partner verification framework covering licences, food-safety permits and training documentation.
Can I book a private chef for a family iftar?

Yes. A private chef cooks and serves a family iftar in your own kitchen, timed to Maghrib. MyCHEF's Arabic specialist, Layla Hassan, builds traditional iftar menus, and you can request a fusion or lighter menu instead.
Do you cater suhoor at home as well?
Yes. Suhoor at home in Dubai is usually a lighter pre-dawn meal, and myCHEF can arrange both iftar and suhoor across Ramadan. Booking both together helps a chef plan the timing across the day.
How far ahead should I book iftar catering?

Book as early as you can. Chefs and caterers fill quickly through Ramadan, especially on weekend evenings, so securing your date well before the month starts gives you the widest choice of chef and menu.

add_block.new_heading: The working day your guests are coming from
new_paragraphs: Iftar planning is scheduling. Private-sector working hours in the UAE reduce by 2 daily during Ramadan under Article 17 of Federal Decree Law No. 33 of 2021 ( UAE government portal ), and normal hours are otherwise 8 a day or 48 a week. Your guests are arriving from a shortened working day, often straight from the office, and the meal is fixed to sunset instead of to an invitation time.

So build the arrival around traffic instead of around the menu. Dates and water need to be ready and reachable the moment guests sit, not carried out after them. Keep the first course something that holds, because arrivals will be staggered by the drive, and plan the substantial food for fifteen to twenty minutes after the call instead of for the instant of it.

add_block.new_heading: What to expect from Ramadan 2026 specifically
new_paragraphs: Two practical points for planning. Ramadan 2026 is expected to begin on 18 or 19 February, subject to the moon-sighting committee, so a date set months ahead may shift by a day — and the working or school day is shortened by 2 hours Monday to Friday, per the The National . Build your guest arrival around the shortened day, and keep the date flexible by a day either side.

The same guidance notes that restaurants and hotels now stay open through daylight hours to accommodate non-fasters, that employers must provide a secluded eating area for those not fasting, and that discretion about eating in public is expected. If your table mixes fasting and non-fasting guests, the courteous setup is somewhere separate and unremarkable for anyone eating before the call, instead of asking them to wait or to sit apart at the meal itself.
